argument_summary: The present record supports only a narrow certification theory. Aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and a 3% rollout with rollback and monitoring show deployment discipline, but the same admissible record also shows the health-plan benefits support segment remains exposed, the segment is below target on benefits-eligibility explanation, and there is no approved risk acceptance covering that exposure. Under the stated policy, rollout controls do not independently cure that gap. The defensible position is therefore not clean present compliance on controls alone, but caveated certification conditioned on explicit disclosure of the named limitation in the model card or equivalent launch materials for the exposed use case.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost argument is needed to resolve the policy question on this record.
claims_about_policy: The policy threshold is specific: when the affected use case remains exposed, rollback, dashboards, monitoring, and a small initial percentage do not remove disclosure duties. On the admissible record, exclusion is absent and approved risk acceptance is absent. That means the only supportable certification rationale in this packet is a caveated one: certification is compliant only if the launch materials explicitly disclose the health-plan benefits support limitation for the named launch use case. The audit concern is valid to the extent it rejects any broader claim that rollout controls alone satisfy policy.
concessions: There is no admissible evidence here proving the final model card or launch documentation already contains the required disclosure.
There is no admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance covering continued exposure of the health-plan benefits support segment.
The rollout design does not exclude the affected segment, so controls alone are insufficient under the policy text.
A clean present-compliance claim would be overbroad on this record.
